risk_if_not_implemented: Without AI Agent Orchestration Protocol Safeguards, AI and autonomous systems may produce unreliable, biased or unsafe outputs, act outside authorized scope, or expose sensitive data. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Privilege Elevation (R-AC-3), AI Output / Decision Integrity Failure (R-AI-1), Unauthorized / Harmful Autonomous Action (R-AI-3), Unintended or Unsafe Technology Behavior (R-AI-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Artificial Intelligence & Autonomous Technologies (AAT) System Failure or Unintended Behavior (MT-13), Adversarial Artificial Intelligence (AI) Attack (MT-29).

compensating_control_1.name: Session Audit
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide session audit capabilities that can: 
(1) Capture and log all content related to a user session; and
(2) Remotely view all content related to an established user session in real time.
compensating_control_1.justification: Session Audit (MON-18.1) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Orchestration Protocol Safeguards (AAT-39.4) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Access Enforcement
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Logical Access Control (LAC) permissions that conform to the principle of "least privilege."
compensating_control_2.justification: Access Enforcement (IAC-25) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Orchestration Protocol Safeguards (AAT-39.4) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
